headline: Google and the FBI seized the NetNut proxy network's two million hijacked home devices as ransomware crews weaponized fresh Citrix and Fortinet flaws and ShinyHunters exposed 3.8 million Medtronic patients.

emerging_trends.text: Coordinated takedowns gathered pace this week as Google and the FBI dismantled the NetNut residential-proxy network while an alleged Scattered Spider member, 19-year-old Peter Stokes, landed in U.S. custody.
emerging_trends.topic_title: NetNut Proxy Network and Popa Botnet Seized

emerging_trends.text: Ransomware affiliates are racing to weaponize freshly disclosed edge-device bugs, with Anubis exploiting CitrixBleed 2 and FortiBleed operators feeding stolen FortiGate credentials to the INC and Lynx gangs.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Ransomware Crews Weaponize Citrix and Fortinet Flaws

emerging_trends.text: Artificial intelligence keeps cutting both ways, as Anthropic's Mythos surfaces open-source flaws, IBM commits $5 billion to fixing them, and Apple compresses its patch cycles because attackers use AI to shrink the time to exploit.
emerging_trends.topic_title: IBM Bets $5 Billion on Anthropic's Bug-Finding AI

topics.title: NetNut Proxy Network and Popa Botnet Seized
topics.latest_developments: The FBI, Google's Threat Intelligence Group, and Lumen seized hundreds of domains and degraded NetNut, also tracked as Popa, cutting its pool of more than two million compromised home devices, roughly two weeks after KrebsOnSecurity tied the service to publicly traded Israeli firm Alarum Technologies (NASDAQ: ALAR).
topics.summary: NetNut rented access to millions of hijacked residential devices so criminals and nation-state actors could mask attack traffic; the disruption strips those relays and exposes the company behind the service.

sources.title: FBI Seizes NetNut Proxy Platform, Popa Botnet
Google, FBI Disrupt NetNut Residential Proxy Network Powered by Millions of Devices
Google Disrupts NetNut Residential Proxy Network Spanning 2 Million Home Devices

topics.title: IBM Bets $5 Billion on Anthropic's Bug-Finding AI
topics.latest_developments: IBM and Red Hat assigned 20,000 engineers to a new Project Lightwell service to fix open-source flaws surfaced by Anthropic's Mythos AI, as the Trump administration lifted restrictions on Claude Fable 5 following a cybersecurity alarm and SecurityWeek detailed Cursor's DuneSlide flaws (CVE-2026-50548, CVE-2026-50549) that enable OS-level remote code execution.
topics.summary: Anthropic's automated bug hunting is reshaping software-supply-chain defense and drawing a multibillion-dollar remediation response, even as AI coding tools like Cursor open new attack surfaces; CISOs should govern AI tool usage and audit generated code before it ships.

sources.title: Anthropic's AI Finds Bugs. IBM Bets $5B It Can Fix Them.
Trump Administration Lifts Restrictions on Anthropic's Claude Models After Cybersecurity Alarm
Critical Cursor AI Code Editor Flaws Could Lead to OS-Level Remote Code Execution

topics.title: PamStealer Targets macOS Passwords
topics.latest_developments: Jamf Threat Labs disclosed PamStealer, a macOS infostealer shipped as a compiled AppleScript file impersonating the open-source Maccy clipboard manager, that abuses pluggable authentication module checks to capture users' login passwords.
topics.summary: Distributed through fake Maccy websites, PamStealer signals mounting investment in Mac infostealers; users should install clipboard tools only from verified sources and treat unexpected password prompts as suspect.

sources.title: PamStealer Uses Fake Maccy Sites and PAM Checks to Steal Mac Login Passwords
Newly discovered PamStealer isn't your typical macOS malware

topics.title: Pegasus Reinfects EU Spyware Investigator
topics.latest_developments: Citizen Lab found that Stelios Kouloglou, a former member of the European Parliament's committee investigating commercial spyware abuses, was infected with NSO Group's Pegasus twice while serving on it.
topics.summary: Researchers describe the targeting of a lawmaker probing spyware as a direct attack on the rule of law, deepening scrutiny of Pegasus deployments against European officials.

sources.title: Spyware found on phone of European Parliament member probing it
EU Politicians Investigated Pegasus Spyware. Then It Ended Up on One of Their Phones

topics.title: Medtronic Breach Exposes 3.8 Million
topics.latest_developments: Medtronic began notifying more than 3.8 million people July 3 that the extortion group ShinyHunters accessed its corporate IT systems in April 2026 and stole personal and medical information.
topics.summary: Medical-device maker Medtronic confirmed the intrusion in late April; affected patients and employees should watch for identity fraud and phishing tied to the exposed health records.

sources.title: Medtronic Data Breach Impacts 3.8 Million People

topics.title: Ransomware Crews Weaponize Citrix and Fortinet Flaws
topics.latest_developments: The Hacker News reported July 2 that Anubis ransomware affiliates now exploit CitrixBleed 2 (CVE-2025-5777) for initial access, while Dark Reading and SecurityWeek tied FortiBleed operators to the INC and Lynx gangs monetizing hundreds of thousands of hijacked FortiGate firewalls and adding a Nextcloud zero-day, as attackers seized on public proof-of-concept code to read NetScaler memory through a newly disclosed CitrixBleed flaw.
topics.summary: Ransomware operators are chaining freshly disclosed Citrix and Fortinet vulnerabilities into intrusions; administrators should patch NetScaler and FortiGate appliances and rotate exposed credentials immediately.

sources.title: Ransomware Groups Turn to Citrix Bleed 2, BYOVD, and Supply Chain Credentials
FortiBleed Actors Collaborating With Inc, Lynx Ransomware Gangs
FortiBleed Campaign Linked to INC, Lynx Ransomware Attacks
New CitrixBleed Vulnerability Exploited Immediately After Public Disclosure

business_politics.title: Cool June Jobs Report Jolts Markets
business_politics.latest_developments: Thursday's weaker-than-expected June U.S. employment report sent a risk-on wave through global markets into July 3, weakening the dollar to a losing week, lifting gold, and pushing Wall Street strategists to reposition around slower hiring.
business_politics.summary: A cooler-than-forecast June jobs report revived expectations of Federal Reserve rate cuts and drove global stocks higher and the WSJ Dollar Index down about 0.5 percent, even as U.S. markets closed for the Independence Day holiday.

sources.title: Weak Jobs Report Prompts Wall Street to Change Strategy
The June jobs report was a blip — we hope

business_politics.title: Canada Advances Pacific Oil Pipeline
business_politics.latest_developments: Canada and Alberta agreed July 2 to back a new crude pipeline from Alberta to British Columbia's Pacific coast, a move to ship roughly one million barrels a day to Asia and cut reliance on U.S. buyers.
business_politics.summary: Prime Minister Mark Carney's government advanced the project to reduce Canada's dependence on the United States as its main oil customer amid trade hostilities, easing Alberta separatist pressure while preserving British Columbia coastal environmental protections.

sources.title: Canada, Alberta Agree to Back New Crude Pipeline to Pacific Coast
Canada unveils plans for new oil pipeline to break dependence on US

business.title: 'Mayor of Kingstown' Wraps Final Season
business.latest_developments: The crime drama 'Mayor of Kingstown' finished shooting its fifth and final season in the Pittsburgh area, KDKA reported July 3, closing out a production the Pittsburgh Film Office values at more than $325 million in local spending.
business.summary: The series filmed across the region since 2022 completed its final season, ending a run the Pittsburgh Film Office credits with over $325 million injected and more than 10,000 jobs created over 457 shoot days.

sources.title: "Mayor of Kingstown" wraps up filming final season in Pittsburgh area

business.title: Trace Brewing Pauses Drag Shows
business.latest_developments: Trace Brewing paused its indoor drag performances, WTAE reported July 3, changing its entertainment lineup amid a dispute with neighbors who complained.
business.summary: The Pittsburgh brewery halted its drag shows after neighbor complaints, reshaping its indoor programming as the disagreement plays out.

sources.title: Trace Brewing pauses drag performances amid dispute with neighbors

around_town.title: Steamy, Stormy Holiday Weekend
around_town.latest_developments: Western Pennsylvania entered a fourth straight day of extreme heat warnings on July 3, with feels-like readings above 100 degrees, and forecasters flagged severe-weather alert days Friday and Saturday and an impact day Sunday as storms move in.
around_town.summary: The extreme heat warning covers most of western Pennsylvania, while the higher elevations of Indiana, Westmoreland, and Fayette counties sit under a heat advisory until 10 p.m. Friday, and afternoon storms threaten the Fourth of July weekend.

sources.title: Fourth straight day of extreme heat warnings in effect for the Pittsburgh area
July 4th Weekend for Western PA: Steamy and stormy

around_town.title: Red Line 'T' Shutdown in Dormont
around_town.latest_developments: Pittsburgh Regional Transit will close a stretch of the Red Line 'T' starting Monday, July 6, halting trains between the Dormont Junction and Potomac stations while crews replace rail crossings at Alabama and Hillsdale avenues in Dormont Borough.
around_town.summary: The construction disrupts Red Line service for riders traveling to and from Pittsburgh, forcing them onto alternatives as crews rebuild the grade crossings.

sources.title: Construction work will disrupt "T" service on PRT's Red Line next week

around_town.title: East Hills Seniors Without Air Conditioning
around_town.latest_developments: Residents of the Marian Plaza Apartments in Pittsburgh's East Hills neighborhood went a seventh straight day without air conditioning on July 3 as the heat wave pushed feels-like temperatures near triple digits.
around_town.summary: Tenants of the subsidized senior housing complex have endured a week of discomfort during one of the year's hottest stretches, with resident Sharon Poslik describing sitting in the dark behind blackout curtains with her lights off.

sources.title: Residents at apartment building in Pittsburgh without air conditioning during heat wave

events.title: Canonsburg Fourth of July Parade
events.latest_developments: Residents began lining the route with chairs on July 3 to claim spots ahead of Canonsburg's 63rd annual Fourth of July parade on Saturday, July 4.
events.summary: The Canonsburg parade, one of Pennsylvania's largest Independence Day celebrations, draws thousands to the Washington County borough, where parade veterans reserve their curbside seats days in advance.

sources.title: Chairs line Canonsburg Fourth of July parade route as residents prepare to celebrate
Thousands prepare to line the streets of Canonsburg for the annual Fourth of July parade

events.title: Pittsburgh Symphony Budget Jumps to $42 Million
events.latest_developments: A July 1 Post-Gazette analysis traced the Pittsburgh Symphony Orchestra's $7 million budget increase, to $42 million, largely to its growing film-music work.
events.summary: The Pittsburgh Symphony Orchestra's annual budget rose by $7 million to $42 million, growth the Post-Gazette attributes in large part to recording and performing film scores.

sources.title: Analysis: Here's why the Pittsburgh Symphony's budget just jumped by $7 million to $42 million

around_teams.title: Hiles Spreads the Blame for Skenes
around_teams.latest_developments: A July 3 Post-Gazette deep dive by Noah Hiles spread responsibility for Paul Skenes's rough stretch beyond the ace himself, weighing the roles of Pirates pitching coaches and catchers.
around_teams.summary: Columnist Noah Hiles examined the causes of Skenes's recent struggles, pointing beyond the pitcher to figures including coaches Marin, Murphy, and catcher Kelly.

sources.title: Noah Hiles: Who's to blame for Paul Skenes' struggles? A deep dive reveals plenty of possibilities

around_teams.title: SNR Drive Digs Into Steelers Offseason Grades
around_teams.latest_developments: On the July 1 Steelers show 'SNR Drive,' analysts Matt Williamson and Wes Uhler combed through ESPN writer Seth Walder's 2026 NFL offseason grades and debated Pittsburgh's marks.
around_teams.summary: The Steelers' team channel broke down Walder's report card for all 32 teams, assessing how the club's roster moves stacked up across the league as training camp nears.

sources.title: NFL Offseason Grades + "Best Of The Wes" | SNR Drive (Jul.1)

team_usa.title: USMNT Draws Belgium, Loses Balogun
team_usa.latest_developments: The United States advances to a World Cup round-of-16 tie with Belgium and will play it without striker Folarin Balogun, whom ESPN reported July 3 cannot appeal his red card against Bosnia and Herzegovina and faces an extended ban.
team_usa.summary: The U.S. men must replace top scorer Balogun against a Belgium side that rallied from two goals down to beat Senegal in extra time, leaving coach Mauricio Pochettino to weigh replacements at forward.

sources.title: How will the USMNT cope without suspended star striker Folarin Balogun?
Sources: USMNT cannot appeal Balogun red card

team_usa.title: Olympic Canoeist Indicted Over Reflecting Pool
team_usa.latest_developments: A grand jury indicted David Hearn, a three-time U.S. Olympic canoeist, on a felony charge July 2 over damage to Washington's Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool that President Trump called vandalism.
team_usa.summary: The indictment accuses Hearn, 67, of maliciously breaking lining material on the pool's bottom on June 19, damage tied to a troubled $14.7 million renovation the president ordered.

sources.title: Ex-Olympian indicted in Reflecting Pool case
US Olympian indicted after Trump alleged 'vandalism' at DC reflecting pool

reading.title: Beware of Productivity Paradoxes
reading.summary: Newport recalls how the personal computer, seemingly a productivity slam dunk with spreadsheets and word processors, delivered murky gains, and he warns readers to expect the same paradox from AI tools.
